name: upstream_status
summary: The upstream did not return a success status, so there is no completed exchange to record.
trigger: The response phase completed and the upstream status was anything other than 200.
grounding: A turn is a completed exchange with a provider; an error response is a record of one failing to happen. Capturing them would put failed requests in the same log as conversations and leave every consumer to re-derive the difference — including the deriver, which projects rows into a conversation tree. Any implementation sees the status, so any implementation can apply this, which is what makes it contract rather than plumbing. Dropping is not silence: the exchange is still reported under this reason, with its status, so the diagnostic value of a failed call survives without a failed call becoming a turn.

examples.description: the completed exchange every provider answers a turn with
a 2xx that is not 200 is still not a completed turn — the rule is the status, not its class
a success carrying no content is not an exchange to record
a malformed request the provider refused

notes: `eligible` means the exchange passes THIS gate, not that it is captured: every later gate still applies. The examples are reached only once the response phase has completed — that lifecycle is stream state rather than data, and is deliberately outside what a case can assert; a status of 0 is `missing_status`, a transport reason, and is not an input here. Both implementations apply this gate: the gateway adapter dispatches only on 200 and records everything else under this reason, and the standalone client refuses to capture a non-200 exchange and logs the reason with the status at a severity an operator sees.
